questions.q: What does 'fat tails' mean when describing the distribution of financial returns?
options: Returns are always positive on average
The distribution has more probability mass in its extreme tails than a Normal distribution would predict
Returns are perfectly symmetric around zero
The variance of returns is exactly zero
questions.explain: Fat tails means extreme moves occur far more frequently than a Normal distribution would predict, reflected in excess kurtosis above the Normal distribution's value of 3.

questions.q: Which stylized fact is ARCH/GARCH modeling (covered in Chapter 4) specifically designed to capture?
options: Aggregational Gaussianity
Volatility clustering — periods of high and low volatility that persist over time
The fact that stock prices never go below zero
Perfect linear predictability of future returns
questions.explain: Volatility clustering — large moves followed by more large moves, calm periods followed by more calm periods — is exactly what GARCH models capture by letting variance depend on past squared returns and past variance.

questions.q: A quant finds that raw log returns show almost no autocorrelation, but squared log returns show strong, slowly decaying autocorrelation. What does this combination indicate?
options: The data must contain errors
Returns are easy to predict but volatility is not
Returns are hard to predict directionally, but volatility is predictable and clusters over time
The asset is not actually traded on a public exchange
questions.explain: Near-zero return autocorrelation is consistent with weak-form market efficiency, while strong squared-return autocorrelation is the statistical signature of volatility clustering.

questions.q: What is the 'leverage effect' in the context of negative skew in equity returns?
options: The tendency of hedge funds to use excessive margin
Falling stock prices mechanically increase a company's debt-to-equity ratio, raising risk and volatility further, reinforcing downside moves
A regulatory rule limiting how much a stock can fall in one day
The effect of options expiration on trading volume
questions.explain: As a stock's price falls, its financial leverage (debt-to-equity) rises mechanically, making the remaining equity riskier — this reinforcing relationship between falling prices and rising volatility produces negative skew.

options: Returns become more Normally distributed as the aggregation horizon lengthens (e.g., daily to monthly)
All financial returns are exactly Gaussian regardless of frequency
Returns become less Normal as more data is collected
A technique for removing outliers from a return series
questions.explain: Aggregational Gaussianity refers to the empirical observation that as returns are aggregated over longer horizons, their distribution looks progressively closer to Normal, due to a central-limit-theorem-like averaging effect.
